title: The Fall of Constantinople
description: April-May 1453. The player commands the last defenders of Byzantium under Constantine XI. Hold the Theodosian Walls against Mehmed II's siege: repair breaches from bombard fire, guard the sea walls along the Golden Horn, and survive repeated assaults. Defeat comes if the Hagia Sophia district falls; victory means holding until the final assault is broken.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN placed as Sultan Mehmed II: Saladin was a Kurdish Ayyubid sultan who died in 1193, 260 years before 1453 and from an entirely different dynasty and army; a generic Turkish hero, a King unit, or a renamed unique unit would have avoided this

CAMEL_RIDER x4 in the Ottoman roster: camel cavalry are not part of the Ottoman siege force at Constantinople (and are not even available to the Turkish civilisation in the engine); the besiegers' shock arm was the sipahi horseman and the Janissary corps
No JANISSARY or HAND_CANNONEER anywhere in the Ottoman army despite these being available in the engine and being the defining Ottoman assault troops of 1453; CHAMPION x6 stands in for them
TREE_PALM_FOREST x6 as the map's vegetation: palm forest belongs to a desert/tropical tileset, not the Thracian and Bosphorus landscape of Constantinople

No water tiles, sea walls, or any naval units despite the Golden Horn / 'ships dragged overland past Galata' narration; the naval beat is delivered by land-unit PATROL triggers, so the Ottoman fleet simply does not exist

Only 2 BOMBARD_CANNON for the famous siege train (Orban's great bombard plus dozens of guns), with MANGONEL x2 filling in — mangonels are period-plausible but understate the gunpowder character of this specific siege

issues_found: Sultan Mehmed II is represented by the SALADIN hero — a 12th-century Kurdish Ayyubid, three centuries and an entirely different polity removed from the Ottoman conqueror of 1453. The engine ships no Mehmed hero, but a renamed generic Champion/Cavalier (as was done for Constantine XI with the KING unit) was available and avoidable.

Both players' civilizations are left as RANDOM, so architecture, unique units and tech are arbitrary — Byzantines and Turks both exist in the engine and would have given Byzantine walls/cataphracts and Turkish janissaries/bombards.
TREE_PALM_FOREST is used for the vegetation around Constantinople; palms are wrong for the Bosphorus/Thrace and cheap alternatives (pine, oak) exist.

Ottoman assault force is built of CAMEL_RIDER x4 and CHAMPION x6 rather than the era-defining janissary infantry; hand cannoneers or elite infantry would have been closer, and camels are not part of the 1453 siege army.

Victory is triggered by killing the enemy leader, which inverts history: Mehmed survived and the city fell. The narration then asserts 'Constantinople stands - the walls of Rome hold once more', a flat counterfactual.

Hagia Sophia is represented by a MONASTERY and the sea walls/Golden Horn are only referenced in text; no water, harbour chain or ship objects appear in the roster to support the 'ships over land' wave, which is delivered by land PATROL actions only.

SALADIN is placed as the Ottoman commander for Mehmed II — a Kurdish Ayyubid sultan of the 1180s standing in for an Ottoman sultan of 1453, an avoidable cross-culture and cross-era error when a renamed generic unit (or a Janissary/Champion named 'Mehmed II') was available

Both players' civilizations are left RANDOM, so architecture sets and unit bonuses may render Byzantines and Ottomans as, e.g., Celts and Vikings; the engine ships both Byzantines and Turks and neither was assigned

The Ottoman assault force uses CHAMPION x6 and CAMEL_RIDER x4 rather than the Turkish Janissary the engine actually ships — janissaries were the signature assault troops of the 1453 storm, and camel riders were not part of the army before Constantinople

The Golden Horn sea-wall theme is narrated ('Mehmed's fleet, dragged overland past Galata... now floats upon the Golden Horn') but there is no water, no dock, and not a single ship placed anywhere on the 120x120 map; Wave 3 is delivered by the same land patrol as the other waves
TREE_PALM_FOREST x6 as the map's only vegetation is wrong for Thrace and the Bosphorus

Only ONAGER x1 and SCORPION x2 plus a Siege Workshop for the defenders, and no Byzantine-specific defensive flavour (e.g., Sea Walls/Harbour, cataphract-type troops); STONE_WALL x124 with GUARD_TOWER x5 and a single KEEP is a thin abstraction of the triple Theodosian line — the inner/outer wall and moat structure is not represented

Victory fires on the death of the enemy commander, producing the counterfactual 'the Ottoman host breaks and flees. Constantinople stands' — the City fell on 29 May 1453 and Mehmed II survived to reign for 28 more years

Hagia Sophia is represented by a MONASTERY that must be destroyed for defeat, but historically Hagia Sophia was never destroyed — it was converted, and the City's fall turned on the breach at the Gate of St. Romanus, not on the church burning
